candidate.body:
Arrange the following categories of share capital in order, beginning with the amount authorised to be issued and ending with the amount actually received from shareholders.
(P) Subscribed Capital
(Q) Authorised Capital
(R) Paid-up Capital
(S) Issued Capital
(T) Called-up Capital
Choose the correct sequence.
candidate.explanation: Authorised capital is the amount the company is authorised to issue; issued capital is part of it, and subscribed capital is part of the issued capital. Called-up capital is part of subscribed capital, while paid-up capital is the amount actually received from shareholders out of the called-up capital. Therefore, the sequence is Q, S, P, T, R.
evidence_quotes: Authorised Capital: Authorised capital is the amount of share capital which a company is authorised to issue by its Memorandum of Association.

Issued Capital: It is that part of the authorised capital which is actually issued to the public for subscription including the shares allotted to vendors and the signatories to the company’s memorandum.
Subscribed Capital: It is that part of the issued capital which has been actually subscribed by the public.

Called up Capital: It is that part of the subscribed capital which has been called up on the shares, i.e., what the company has asked the shareholders to pay. The company may decide to call the entire amount or part of the face value of the shares, For example, if the face value (also called nominal value) of a share allotted is Rs. 10 and the company has called up only Rs. 7 per share, in that scenario, the called up capital is Rs. 7 per share. The remaining Rs. 3 may be collected from its shareholders as and when needed. Paid up Capital: It is that portion of the called up capital which has been actually received from the shareholders.
stated_assumptions: Interpret the order as the successive relationship between the categories in the definitions, not as a chronology of transactions.
Only the five listed categories are to be arranged.
option_analysis: Incorrect: subscribed capital is part of issued capital, so issued capital must precede it.
Incorrect: issued capital is part of authorised capital, so authorised capital must precede it.
Correct: the definitions establish the chain authorised, issued, subscribed, called-up, and paid-up capital.
Incorrect: paid-up capital is part of called-up capital, so called-up capital must precede it.

candidate.body: In a fixed-price, two-sector model with no indirect taxes, subsidies or other leakages, autonomous expenditure increases by ₹15 lakh.
